title: A framework for the etiology of running-related injuries
authors: Bertelsen ML, Hulme A, Petersen J, Brund RK, Sorensen H, Finch CF, Parner ET, Nielsen RO
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: Runners in general; an evidence-informed conceptual framework with no original data and no sample
findings: The article presents a conceptual framework for the multifactorial etiology of running-related injury in four mutually exclusive parts: (a) structure-specific capacity when entering a running session; (b) structure-specific cumulative load per running session; (c) reduction in the structure-specific capacity during a session; and (d) exceeding the structure-specific capacity.

The authors propose that the framework inform the design of prevention studies, including research questions, hypotheses and the monitoring of participation-related and non-participation-related exposures.

They state that future research should address how changes in one or more exposures influence injury risk, which needs study of how different factors affect structure-specific load and load capacity, and of the dose-response relationship between running participation and injury risk, so as to move beyond traditional risk-factor identification.
limitations: A conceptual framework, not a study: it has no data, no thresholds and no estimate of how capacity changes over time or after a break, and it is not tested in the abstract. Its value is a way of stating the question (capacity against load, per structure), not an answer. Abstract read; full text not read.
implications: Gives the frame in which a past training block can be discussed: it may bear on the capacity of a structure, while the load of a session is what that capacity is set against. A runner's total minutes do not show the capacity of any one structure.
No rule, rate or Param follows from it; the authors themselves call the dose-response relationship between running participation and injury risk a matter for future research.
